chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Do not swear by Allah as truthful and not as liars, for He (Exalted and Glorious) says: "And do not make Allah an excuse for your oaths."'
ai.seo_question: What is the proper way to swear an oath in Islam according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the theological nuance of the Quranic command 'Do not make Allah an excuse for your oaths' (2:224), warning against swearing by Allah in a manner that treats His name as a mere instrument for one's own truthfulness or falsehood. This instruction underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on preserving the sanctity of the Divine Name, ensuring that oaths reflect genuine reverence rather than casual utility, thereby preventing the trivialization of Allah's majesty in daily discourse.
